newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler's Eaton sees dollar at 110-118 yen.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler's Eaton sees dollar at 110-118 yen.

text.p: Chrysler Corp chairman Robert Eaton said on Monday he believed the U.S. dollar would continue to be worth 110 to 118 yen through 1997, and then drop off to 100 sometime next year.

Eaton told the Automotive News World Congress that the Bank of Japan had been buying dollars and ordering other Japanese banks to hold dollar assets, thus allowing Japan to suppress the value of the yen.

A weaker yen gives Japanese automakers a cost advantage over the Big Three because they can export vehicles more cheaply. Eaton and the heads of Detroit's other Big Three automakers recently travelled to Washington D.C. to complain to U.S. government officials about Japan's action.
"We wanted our government to protest (against) the Bank of Japan's manipulation of the yen," he said on Monday.

In addition to the yen, Eaton said he had two other concerns as he looked out through 1997: government regulation and the state of the economy. Regulation could easily cause the third largest U.S. automaker problems, said Eaton, citing proposed new airbag rules as one example.

Eaton said Chrysler would probably offer a cut-off switch in vehicles with a bench seat in the front later this year. The switch would allow customers to de-activate the passenger side airbag. Safety advocates have demanded that automakers take action such as reducing the deployment force of airbags because they can kill children and small adults.
Commenting on the economy, Eaton said, "We don't see any dark clouds out there, but we know they're out there."

On other matters, Eaton said Chrysler "could not be more pleased" with the reception its concept and production vehicles were receiving at the North American International Auto Show, which opened to the public on January 11.
"There are a couple of (concepts) out there that probably could be built, but I'm not going to tell you which ones," he said.
